citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
Records show "Leaf" a two-year-old intact Mule Deer was fed toxic browse, unintentionally, as part of his diet by a staff
member 6/20 – 6/22/26. Leaf’s medical records indicate by 6/22/26 he lost interest in food, on 6/23 experienced digestive
issues, on 6/24 his energy was low, on 6/25/appeared dehydrated, had a low-grade fever, had moderately swollen joints,
and weighed 56lbs. He was given an NSAID for pain and inflammation that afternoon prescribed by the attending
veterinarian (AV). Records show Leaf did not receive an in-person veterinary health assessment for 4 days after the onset
of symptoms. The facility representative stated their hoof stock veterinarian was not available and they had to locate a
backup veterinarian with hoof stock experience. A veterinarian came to the facility and assessed and treated Leaf on
6/26/26. The delay in providing veterinary care may have caused unnecessary pain and discomfort to the mule deer.
Each exhibitor shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include the availability of
appropriate facilities, personnel, equipment, and services to comply with the provisions of this subchapter.
To be corrected from this day forward, July 24, 2026

Records show "Leaf" a two-year-old intact Mule Deer, was fed toxic browse, unintentionally, by a staff member, as part of
his diet 6/20 – 6/22/26. Leaf’s medical records indicate by 6/22/26 he lost interest in food, on 6/23 experienced digestive
disturbances, on 6/24 his energy was low, and on 6/25/ he appeared dehydrated, had a low-grade fever, had moderately
swollen joints, and weighed 56 lbs. He was given an NSAID for pain and inflammation prescribed by the AV that
afternoon, and a veterinarian came to the facility and assessed and treated Leaf the following day, 6/26/26.
Prior to Leaf being fed toxic browse, and after his recovery, the veterinarian stated the diet and feeding directions,
prescribed by her, were not consistently followed.
The veterinary exam report dated 7/22/26 states Leaf’s diet was found to be inappropriate and insufficient. The
veterinarian stated these factors have contributed to his weight loss and are documented in the veterinary exam report
dated 07/12/2026. It reports that in April 2026, Leaf weighed 71 lbs. The veterinary exam report dated 7/22/26 states that
his weight as of 7/20/26 was down to 56.4 lbs.
Feeding an inappropriate diet to animals can negatively affect their health and well-being. The food shall be wholesome,
palatable, and free from contamination and of sufficient quantity and nutritive value to maintain all animals in good health.
The diet shall be prepared with consideration for the age, species, condition, size, and type of animal.
To be corrected from this day forward July 24, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
